title: Model fragmentation heatmap and procurement trigger canvas
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Background: Teams building RAG/long-context and streaming features have reported fragility when models change (variants, quantization, tokenizer differences). Current model-watch efforts surface new model releases but lack a decision canvas linking technical fragmentation (compatibility gaps) to procurement actions. Goal: deliver an evidence-backed heatmap that scores model fragmentation across workload archetypes and a procurement trigger canvas that maps observable signals to recommended negotiations or reserved-capacity actions.

Scope:
- Define fragmentation taxonomy for three workload archetypes: long-context RAG (>=32k tokens), streaming/low-latency generation, and high-throughput embeddings/search.
- Build a heatmap (fragmentation vs. regional availability) covering top 18 open and commercial model families we track.
- Produce a trigger canvas (decision table) that prescribes actions (e.g., secure reserved capacity, negotiate license fallback, enable quantization fallback test) given signal thresholds.
- Deliver an initial dashboard (Looker/LookML or internal console tab) and a one-page exec summary + recommended procurement SLAs.

Methodology:
1) Signal collection: monthly crawl of model registries, vendor release notes, and community forks; ingest into the model-signals table (schema v1: model_id, variant, quantized_formats, tokenizer_family, region_availability, license_type, release_date, latency_samples, fail_rate_by_workload). Data team ticket: GH-ops/model-signals-import (linked below).
2) Synthetic evaluation: run three synthetic suites per archetype (long-context RAG stress with prefix caching, streaming microburst latency, batched embeddings throughput). Capture latency p95/p99, token cost delta, and correctness regression vs. pinned baseline.
3) Compatibility scoring: automated heuristics produce a fragmentation score (0-100) combining variant count, tokenizer drift score, quantization gaps, and observed correctness regressions.
4) Procurement trigger rules: create a risk model that combines fragmentation score, region scarcity index, and cost delta to compute a trigger severity (none / monitor / engage procurement / reserve capacity).

Deliverables:
- Heatmap CSV and Looker dashboard: model_fragmentation_heatmap_v1.csv + Looker dashboard link.
- Procurement trigger canvas (PDF) with detailed decision rules and threshold rationale.
- Implementation plan for integrating triggers into Growth & Sales procurement workflows (contact: @legal and @sales-ops).

Acceptance criteria:
- Heatmap covers at least 18 models and 3 archetypes with documented data sources.
- Trigger canvas includes actionable next steps and mapping to procurement contacts.
- Dashboard is queryable by model, region, and archetype with filters for release date and license type.
- Repro pipeline (scripts + data schema) checked into GH repo and test run completes end-to-end on CI for one model family.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence PRD (draft): https://company-confluence.internal/redwood/ModelFragmentationPRD
- Shared folder (workbook, CSVs): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-ModelHeatmap
- GitHub proto (signals + scoring): https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-signals-proto/pull/27
- Synthetic eval dashboard (internal): https://dash.redwood.internal/model-evals/frag-v1

Trade-offs & notes:
- We prioritize coverage for workload archetypes that drive high revenue (RAG + embeddings). This reduces initial breadth but increases signal quality where it matters most.
- Scoring heuristics will be intentionally conservative; early thresholds tilt toward false positives (engage procurement) to avoid customer outages. We will tune thresholds after one month of telemetry.
- Privacy/legal: license_type extraction may be noisy for some community forks; manual verification step included for high-impact models.

Stakeholders: Product (Maya + Diego), Research (Linnea Wong), Data (Oliver Chen), Legal (Asha Patel), Sales Ops (Ethan Brooks).
